children: shares climbed 4% in early Thursday after the drugmaker reported stronger-than-expected third-quarter results and raised its 2026 financial targets.

Revenue increased 39% from a year earlier to $24.4 billion, exceeding analyst estimates of approximately $22.4 billion to $22.6 billion. Adjusted earnings reached $7.48 per share, also surpassing Wall Street expectations.

The company's diabetes and weight-management medicines remained major contributors to growth. Mounjaro generated $10.7 billion in quarterly sales, up 65% year over year, while Zepbound revenue rose 48% to $5.3 billion. Their performance reflects continued demand for treatments targeting diabetes and obesity.

Lilly now expects 2026 revenue of $91 billion to $92 billion, compared with its previous outlook. The company also raised its adjusted earnings-per-share forecast to a range of $35 to $36. The updated targets indicate management expects sales momentum to continue through the remainder of the year.

The results provide fresh evidence of Lilly's ability to translate demand for its leading medicines into revenue growth. Investors will be watching whether prescription trends and production capacity can support the company's higher financial targets in coming quarters.

title: Eli Lilly Stock Jumps on Q3 Earnings Beat
